source.title: GAIA-1: A Generative World Model for Autonomous Driving
source.authors: Anthony Hu; Lloyd Russell; Hudson Yeo; Zak Murez; George Fedoseev; Alex Kendall; Jamie Shotton; Gianluca Corrado

record.file_problem: None; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests scaling behavior in a new setting: a visual, video-token world model trained on driving data.
record.gate_note: The study reports held-out cross-entropy scaling and an extrapolation for GAIA-1. The training-loss curves in Figure 8b are used to fit the scaling relationship; they are not a separate held-out-loss result. Claims about language-model scaling laws cited from other work are not results of this study.
record.test_reason: Section 6 fits a power law (with an irreducible-loss offset) to the held-out validation cross-entropy of smaller autoregressive video-token world models. It then checks that the fit predicts the 6.5B GAIA-1 model. This is the scaling-law method applied in a new modality (driving video), so it bears on V5.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors say scaling laws analogous to those of LLMs apply to GAIA-1, and that models trained with under 20x less compute predict its final cross-entropy accurately. They add that the extrapolation suggests substantial room for improvement from more data and compute.
record.recipe_differences: Uses next-token prediction and a power-law fit to held-out cross-entropy, but applies them to discretized driving video in a world model rather than a language model.
record.problems: The reported extrapolation is described as high accuracy but has no numerical error or uncertainty stated in the text; the plotted values are not given numerically.

untested.parts: Image-only models, repeated data, fine-tuning and transfer are not tested. The scaling of the 2.6B video diffusion decoder is asserted from cited work, not measured. Only compute (estimated as 6N per token) is varied; separate parameter or data scaling is not reported.

record.verdict_notes: This is a model-introduction paper; the scaling result is a short section (Section 6, Figure 8). Figure 8b shows training-loss curves for the fit models, not a separate held-out result. Weaknesses: one held-out target point, no reported prediction error, and no seeds or uncertainty. The extrapolation span (about one order of magnitude) is modest, so the support also bears weakly on extrapolation in a non-text setting. V2 itself names language-model runs, so it is not labelled.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test language-model loss scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute.
The extrapolation is for a visual world model, not language-model runs.
No fixed-compute allocation between parameters and tokens is tested.
No comparison of architecture shape at fixed parameter count is reported.
Tests a video-token world model trained on driving data; does not test other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer.
No downstream task performance or its relationship to pretraining loss is measured.
No sensitivity to fitting choices or systematic departures from the fitted curve is tested.

rows.subject: GAIA-1 world model
rows.operation_detail: Fit a power law to smaller-model results and compare its extrapolation with the final held-out validation cross-entropy.

conditions.value: 0.65M to 650M parameters; 10,000x to 10x smaller than GAIA-1

rows.baseline: Power-law prediction fitted to smaller models
rows.value: The final cross-entropy of GAIA-1 could be predicted with high accuracy; numerical value not stated (Figure 8a).
rows.note: The text describes the extrapolation as accurate, but the plotted values are not provided numerically.
rows.check: Row is correct. Two clarifications: the fit models (0.65M–650M parameters) used up to 1/20 of GAIA-1's compute, so the extrapolation spans only about 10x in parameters and under 20x in compute (roughly one order of magnitude). The fit's compute axis covers about 1e16–1e22 FLOPs per Figure 8a. Accuracy is stated only in words; no error value or uncertainty is given, and the evidence is one figure with one held-out target point.

relationships.condition: Autoregressive transformer world model on discretised driving video (London data); held-out geofenced validation cross-entropy; models 0.65M–6.5B parameters
relationships.reason: A power law f(x)=c+(x/a)^b fitted to the smaller models is reported to predict GAIA-1's final validation cross-entropy with high accuracy (R1). The extrapolation is only about 10–20x and no numerical error is given.
relationships.display_finding: A power law plus constant fitted to smaller models reportedly predicted final GAIA-1 validation cross-entropy accurately over an approximately 10–20-fold extrapolation.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
